title: Dual-mode shim for progressive deprecation of streaming toolcall contracts
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Background: We are deprecating the legacy streaming-toolcall contract (implicit chunked tool responses + inline metadata) in favor of an explicit toolcall streaming protocol (separate tool event stream + structured finish markers). Several customers and SDKs still rely on the legacy contract and cannot update in a single wave.

Proposal: Implement a dual-mode runtime shim that can operate in three modes: legacy-only (current behavior), dual-mode (runtime accepts legacy or new streaming contract and emits both forms to downstream SDKs via adapters), and strict-new (rejects legacy inputs). The shim will be toggleable via a per-route behavior flag and support gradual rollout by routing policy. The shim performs: runtime-side translation, a replayable compatibility log for auditing, and a safe rollback delegate that forwards to legacy runtime paths if translation errors occur.

Goals:
- Allow clients to opt into the new contract while keeping production traffic serving legacy clients.
- Provide a migration path that enables shadowing, gradual opt-in, and fast rollback without customer-visible regressions.
- Capture telemetry to identify regression in structured outputs and streaming boundaries.
- Keep latency overhead per request < 5% for typical 512-token sessions.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change SDK-level public surface; SDK adapters will be separate PM tickets.
- Not addressing embedding or non-streaming toolcall semantics in this work.
tasks: Design shim API and behavior flag schema (per-route + global override)
Implement runtime translator: legacy-stream -> canonical tool-events (and back for compatibility echoes)
Add per-request compatibility header and replayable compatibility log (append-only)
Implement fallback delegate path that forwards to legacy code path on translator errors
Add telemetry hooks: translation success/failure, latency delta, token deviations, structured output diffs
Expose a CLI/Console toggle for dual-mode with rollout percentage and canary routing
Write integration tests and regression replayer harness for streaming sessions
Document migration guide for PM/SDK teams and customer-facing notes
acceptance_criteria: Runtime supports legacy-only, dual-mode, and strict-new modes configurable per-route
Translation error rate in canary <= 0.1% and can be triaged via logs
End-to-end latency overhead <= 5% on representative benchmark (512-token median session)
Regression replayer can reproduce legacy streams and compare structured outputs automatically
Rollout toggle available in Console with percentage and immediate rollback
Security review completed and no plaintext leaks in compatibility logs (KMS enforced)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Canary in dual-mode on internal routes (1% traffic) + run replayer for 48h. Phase 2: Expand to customer beta cohorts (10% traffic) and open SDK adapters for preview. Phase 3: Default new customers to strict-new after 6 weeks unless opt-out. Phase 4: Schedule legacy-only sunsetting with PM communication and final cutoff 3 months after strict-new default.
telemetry: trace: request-span includes translation and fallback delegate segments
testing_plan: Unit: translator parsing/serialization fuzz tests for edge cases (nested tools, garbled markers)
Integration: dual-mode acceptance tests (legacy client -> new server and vice versa)
Regression: replayer harness that runs recorded legacy sessions through new translator and diffs outputs
Load: 512-token synthetic sessions at 2x expected concurrency to verify latency overhead
Chaos: force translator failures to validate fallback delegate and observe no customer-visible errors
implementation_notes: Translator is implemented as a middleware in the request pipeline before batching. Use existing KV cache interfaces for prefix preservation. For translation algorithm, prefer deterministic boundary markers and strict JSON schema validation for tool-call structs. Compatibility log writes go to an encrypted append-only store; use existing KMS integration and redact PII. Keep translation as an incremental opt-in via feature flagging framework used by infra team.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected structured output mismatches causing customer regressions -> Mitigation: initial Canary + automated diff alerts + safe rollback delegate
Risk: Latency regressions at high concurrency -> Mitigation: microbench and optimize critical path, add batching pass-through for dual-mode
Risk: Compatibility log storage cost -> Mitigation: compress and sample logs, 90d retention and retention policy configurable per-customer
Risk: SDK adapters lag behind runtime -> Mitigation: provide clear migration guide and test vectors; coordinate PM and SDK owners
comments: 2025-02-16 Ayesha Patel: Initial ticket created after design sync with PM and SDK. Ran through edge-case list: nested toolcalls, partial chunking, and out-of-order tool events.

2025-02-20 Marco Li: Implemented initial translator prototype (branch runtime/dual-mode-proto). Found mismatches in multi-tool stream where finish marker was omitted; added heuristic to close open tool sessions at end-of-stream.
2025-02-26 Priya Nair (SDK): Reviewed translator events. SDK adapters will need a 'compat_echo' mode to accept both event shapes. We'll open a separate SDK ticket to coordinate.

2025-03-01 Omar Hassan (Security): Reviewed logging design. Compatibility log must be encrypted with customer KMS; added requirement to strip user PII. Security review started and pending remediation on retention policy.
2025-03-04 Marco Li: Added fallback delegate and tests. Canary scheduled for 2025-03-07 on internal cohort. Benchmarks show ~3.2% median latency overhead for 512-token sessions.
